subject: Live delivery degradation — sustained chunk timeouts causing client stalls
messages:
From: Alyssa Gomez <ops@aperture.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@aperture.ai
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Increased websocket timeouts and chunk drops affecting prod live mode

Jonas —

We started seeing a surge in client-visible timeouts in our production live feature at ~08:45 PT. Symptoms: clients see streaming sessions freeze for ~10-30s, then large gaps in token delivery (partial chunks) followed by multi-chunk bursts. Error rate (5xx from your API) has risen from ~0.3% baseline to ~6% for the past 30m. Throughput has dropped ~40% for the two largest endpoints.

We captured session IDs and a pcap during the incident and are attaching logs. We're in a P0 on our side — customers are hitting SLOs and some workflows are aborting. Can Redwood confirm whether this is a degraded region, proxy bottleneck, or a model-side stall?

Sample session: session_id=ap-9c2f-20280628-0812
Top symptom: a sequence of small (<=128B) chunk frames followed by a 15s silence and then a compressed burst that overwhelms the client-side buffer.

Attachments: aperture_logs_0628.zip (traces + request ids), capture_aperture_0628.pcap

Please triage immediately — we will escalate to our execs if this is not contained in the next hour.

Thanks,
Alyssa Gomez
Ops Lead, Aperture AI
ops@aperture.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Gomez <ops@aperture.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 09:22:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Increased websocket timeouts and chunk drops affecting prod live mode

Alyssa —

Thanks for the quick heads up and for the artifacts. I’m pulling infra and runtime on a hot-join. Initial ask for you: can you highlight 2-3 failing request IDs from the logs (or paste them inline) so we can correlate traces? I’ll start with a few mitigations we can toggle without a deploy:

- Route your traffic to our secondary us-west-2 pool (we can switch routing policy TTL to 30s)
- Force model fallback to the smaller variant (temp) to see if chunkization pattern changes
- Increase proxy chunk buffer and disable prefix-KV caching for your account (we can do these from the control plane)

I’ve opened a PagerDuty incident and looped in CS so they can manage the revenue escalation. Priyom — can you lead triage on proxy/ingress? Vanessa — can you own customer comms and confirm whether they want an immediate region failover? Marissa — please prepare a short customer-facing summary for execs.

Jonas
Engineering, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Gomez <ops@aperture.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 09:35:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Increased websocket timeouts and chunk drops affecting prod live mode

Quick triage from infra: early hypothesis is ingress proxy buffer pressure combined with a bursty upstream from the runtime that leads to many sub-128B frames (too small to flush) followed by a backpressure-induced stall. We’re seeing a correlation between increased small-frame frequency and transient epoll wakeups on the proxy.

Immediate actions applied (rolled 09:30 PT):
- Bumped NGINX-ingress proxy chunk buffer to 64k
- Enabled conservative write coalescing on the proxy (experimental flag)
- Temporarily disabled client-level KV prefetch for Aperture account

Telemetry: error rate dropped to ~3.2% after the changes, but we still see 5-10s silent windows for a subset of sessions. Attached quick trace: ingress_trace_0628.txt (inline snippet below).

Suggested next steps:
- If customer approves, route Aperture to us-west-2-secondary to avoid potential overloaded host groups
- Capture expanded runtime logs for sequences where the silent window occurs (we need full stack frames for those request ids)

--Priyom
Prod Infra
priyom.das@redwood.ai

Attachment: ingress_trace_0628.txt

From: Alyssa Gomez <ops@aperture.ai>

Thanks — we toggled the routing to us-west-2-secondary at 09:40 PT. We still see intermittent stalls on ~7% of live sessions; the client-side logs show the same pattern: small chunk, silence, burst. Sample failing request ids: ap-9c2f-20280628-0812, ap-9c2f-20280628-0837, ap-9c2f-20280628-0911.

This is now an executive-level incident for us — it’s affecting scheduled demos and a paid processing pipeline. Our CTO is asking for a short executive summary and for your leadership to be on a call in 30 minutes if the issue isn’t contained. We’d like to avoid a complete failover if possible but need a reliable mitigation.

Alyssa
Aperture AI

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 10:18:09 -0700
Subject: Escalation to execs: Aperture live-delivery degradation — request: exec sync in 30m

Michael / Mina —

We have an active escalation with Aperture AI (large customer, paid production traffic). Symptoms: sustained websocket/chunked-transfer silent windows (5–15s), elevated 5xx rate (~4–6% at peak), and ~40% throughput reduction for the live endpoints. We have applied ingress mitigations (proxy buffer bump, write coalescing, KV prefetch off) — partial improvement but intermittent stalls persist. Customer has routed to secondary but still sees ~7% affected sessions.

Impact: revenue/SLAs for Aperture, executive attention on their side. They’ve shared request ids for correlation. We believe the most likely root cause is a combination of small-frame generation in the runtime + opportunistic proxy coalescing that produces dead windows under certain TCP pacing conditions.

Request: please join a 30-minute war room at 10:50 PT to decide whether to perform a targeted runtime rollback, force a model-variant fallback account-wide, or accept a temporary region failover. PagerDuty incident: PD12345678.

Attachments: aperture_logs_0628.zip (full traces), capture_aperture_0628.pcap

Jonas Weber
Director, Serving Runtime
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Gomez <ops@aperture.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Postmortem: live delivery incident (June 28) — summary and next steps

Alyssa / team —

Thanks again for your patience while we worked through this. Summary of timeline and conclusions:

- 2028-06-28 08:45 PT: customer-reported client stalls and elevated 5xx.
- 2028-06-28 09:30 PT: ingress mitigations applied; partial improvement.
- 2028-06-28 09:40 PT: traffic routed to us-west-2-secondary; incidents continued for ~7% of sessions.
- 2028-06-29: runtime team reproduced small-frame->silent-window pattern in a synthetic harness; root cause was an interaction between a recent write coalescing optimization in the runtime and some kernel-level Nagle-like behavior on our proxy hosts.

Actions taken:
- Reverted the runtime coalescing optimization (rolled 06-29 03:15 PT) — full reduction in silent windows observed in canaries.
- Added a proxy-level safety guard to flush small frames immediately for accounts with live streaming traffic (deployed 06-29 05:00 PT).
- Implemented a customer-specific temporary policy to prefer model variant B for live sessions and to lower proxy buffering thresholds.

Follow-ups:
- We will add a targeted regression test to the release pipeline for write coalescing that includes TCP pacing scenarios (owner: Priyom, due 2028-07-15).
- CS will coordinate a customer-facing RFC describing the fix and a credit adjustment for impacted windows (owner: Marissa).

Alyssa — I’ll follow up with a short executive note you can share with your CTO and customers. If you want a 1:1 briefing, we’re available.

—Marissa Cole
Customer Success
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
